title: Transdiagnostic Quantitative EEG Assessment in a Long-Term Psychiatric Cohort
summary: For mental illnesses, there are so far no objective measurements that help with diagnosis or with choosing the right treatment. A brain wave recording can measure the electrical activity of the brain through sensors on the scalp. The recording is painless, safe and takes about 30 minutes. Previous studies have shown that brain activity can change in various mental illnesses, but these studies were mostly too small to draw reliable conclusions. In this study, we therefore record brain waves at rest in many patients of our hospital and in healthy comparison persons, always following the same procedure. In some patients, we repeat the recording during their treatment or add short tasks with sounds and pictures. We want to find out whether certain patterns of brain activity are related to symptoms, the course of the illness or the response to treatment. The participants’ treatment is not changed by the study.
conditions: Mental and behavioural disorders (transdiagnostic); main focus: depressive disorders (F32/F33) and schizophrenia-spectrum disorders (F20–F29)

interventions.name: Patients (approx. 1000) receiving inpatient, day-clinic or outpatient psychiatric treatment. Single standardized resting-state EEG recording (5 minutes eyes closed and 5 minutes eyes open, approx. 30 minutes) with a wireless dry-electrode EEG system as early as possible in the course of treatment. I

Healthy control participants (up to 200) without current or past psychiatric or neurological disorder. Single standardized resting-state EEG recording following the same protocol as in Arm 1, optionally complemented by the same task-based EEG paradigms.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
●	Adult patients older than 18 years old presenting for psychiatric inpatient or outpatient care at the Klinik und Poliklinik für Psychiatrie und Psychotherapie, TUM Klinikum rechts der Isar or healthy control volunteers meeting the matching/eligibility criteria 
●	Sufficient command of the German or English language to understand the study information and the instructions during the recording
●	Capacity to give informed consent and written informed consent
Exclusion criteria:
●	Current seizure disorder or epilepsy 
●	Subjects without a scalp suitable for sensor contact, or with a sensitive dermatological condition causing sensor intolerance
●	Open wounds or scalp infections
●	Acute substance intoxication at time of recording, or  lack of minimum required cooperation 

●	For healthy controls only: current or past psychiatric or neurological disorder, or current intake of psychotropic medication (self-report)
